Quick answers up front:
- We will attach a diagram that shows hosted (shared control plane + model-serving clusters), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools per tenant), and Private (customer-managed VPC) views. Enforcement points (network ACLs, sidecar policies, control-plane demarcation) will be annotated.

Aisha / Priyom — quick technical notes and proposed attachments (draft):

Attachments: northstar_tenant_coexistence_diagram_v1.png, egress_policy_matrix_v1.pdf, audit_trace_samples_2025-11.csv

Summary answers:
- Tenant boundaries: enforcement occurs at three layers — network (VPC/NSG + per-tenant subnets), runtime (process isolation + tenant-scoped sandboxes), and control plane (RBAC + per-tenant resource scoping). For Hosted we use tenant routing IDs at the load-balancer and sidecar; for Dedicated the GPU pools are isolated by hypervisor/cluster slices; for Private deployments customers manage the VPC and we enforce strict ingress/egress policies and optional host-level attestation.

- KV/cache isolation: the runtime implements namespacing by combining tenant ID + model version + prefix salt — keys are opaque to other tenants. KV stores used (in Dedicated/Private) are either per-tenant instances or use encryption-at-rest with per-tenant KMS keys and enforced access policies. We also validate KV read/write paths in the CI test matrix to catch misrouting.

- Threat scenarios & mitigations (short):
  * Scenario A: misrouted request populates a shared KV with attacker-controlled key — Mitigations: tenant namespacing, write validation, CI tests, periodic cache scrub jobs, and alerting on anomalous cache access patterns.
  * Scenario B: compromised operator host attempts lateral RPC into serving nodes — Mitigations: host attestation, mTLS with short-lived certs, strict host firewall policies, and canarying/failsafe routing that forces degraded but safe execution paths.

- Evidence and telemetry: we can provide sanitized VPC flow logs, per-request provenance headers (route_id, tenant_id, request_ts, model_variant), control-plane audit logs that show role-granted actions, and a sample trace. The CSV contains an anonymized subset of request provenance fields.

I reviewed the diagram; it has three stacked views (hosted/dedicated/private) and highlights enforcement points. Priyom — I added a short paragraph on attestations in the PDF.
